acceptance_for_this_package.success: in one macOS session on the target: 8086:4680 with the recorded binaries, GPU executes the varying workloads, every output word compares, COMPUTE_READBACK_VERIFIED is printed before teardown, the process exits 0 and the system shows no panic, hang or GPU timeout

recovery_entry_check.finding: the machine currently boots with -nvoff, so the driver is disabled by the live boot configuration; the package's config.safe.plist is byte identical to that live config, config.test.plist drops -nvoff to enable the driver, and reference-efi/config.optout-reference.plist keeps a no-GPU reference for recovery. The delivery itself modified no boot file.

refusals_before_any_gpu_work: Run-UHD770-Test.command refuses without root, without /bin/bash -p, on a non-Darwin host, or before PREPARED (missing installed coordinator)
session.sh test refuses when the current boot is not the preparation boot that was armed
session.sh test refuses on an opt-out boot by matching -nvoff in kern.bootargs, and records next_boot_optout=verified only after restore_optout succeeds
session-user.sh manual refuses without nmxintel=1, without an armed state, without a root-owned per-boot authorization naming this uid, and when the recovery marker says NOT_VERIFIED
session-user.sh manual refuses a second manual session in the same boot, so an incomplete run cannot be repeated by accident

pre_compute_gates.recovery: restore_optout writes the safe config to config.plist.uhd770-pending, re-hashes it, atomically renames it into place, re-hashes and syncs; a config changed independently is preserved and the step fails
pre_compute_gates.recorder: Root restarts the persistent capture job and waits for it to confirm startup before the compute phase
pre_compute_gates.driver: session-user.sh waits up to 330 seconds for next_boot_optout=verified and for IORegistry to show NMXGPU in a ready state, with distinct exits for deadline (124), unverified recovery (65), failed initialization (66), registry failure (67) and gate timeout (68)

log_capture: Start-UHD770.command captures from its first command, including failures before the plan exists, and records the exact ancestor permissions that broke earlier attempts without changing them
it copies the preparation log to a USB volume only when exactly one mounted volume carries this package's exact safe or test EFI bytes; otherwise it keeps the system-disk report and says so
session-user.sh takes a per-boot directory as an atomic lock and writes coordinator_exit into the session record
limits: this is a reading of the scripts, not a run; only the target boot shows which configuration OpenCore applied
if the machine panicked before the boot-time restore, the USB could still hold the test config; reference-efi/config.optout-reference.plist and Restore-UHD770.ps1 are the Windows-side recovery

swallowed_error_audit.method: every '|| :' and '|| true' in the packaged session.sh was read, and session-user.sh was checked for the same pattern
categories: evidence collection that is allowed to fail: ls/stat context, sysctl boot identity, kmutil showloaded, dmesg and ioreg snapshots, ditto of the managed directory
best-effort cleanup: bootout of the capture job, killing the log follower, rmdir of the session lock
one automatic export attempt that the user can repeat by hand
swallowed_error_audit.conclusion: no safety-relevant step is swallowed: restore_optout, the recovery verification and the compute sequence all have explicit error handling, so a failure there stops the run instead of degrading quietly
swallowed_error_audit.limit: reading the scripts, not running them

probe_math_check.method: compared the compute shader in the packaged probe with the CPU expectation in the same probe source
probe_math_check.shader: value = input[i] ^ seed; shift = (i % 31) + 1; rotated = (value << shift) | (value >> (32 - shift)); out[i] = (rotated + i * 0x9e3779b9) ^ (input[i] >> 7)
probe_math_check.cpu: same expression, with input[i] produced by seed ^ (i * 747796405 + 2891336453)
probe_math_check.finding: the GPU and CPU formulas are identical term by term, including that the final xor uses the unrotated input, and the shift stays in 1..31 so no undefined shift can occur; the dispatch covers ceil(count/64) groups of 64 invocations and the probe bounds-checks i against count
probe_math_check.synchronization: host->compute and compute->host pipeline barriers bracket the dispatch, and the readback invalidates non-coherent memory before comparing
probe_math_check.limits: this shows the probe would detect a wrong result rather than agreeing with itself; it does not show the GPU ran

kext_loading_check.method: parsed the packaged kext Info.plist and Mach-O header, and read what the CI preflight actually runs

personality.NMXGPUIntel: IOProviderClass IOPCIDevice, IOPCIPrimaryMatch 0x00008086 & 0x0000ffff (any Intel vendor), IOPCIClassMatch 0x03000000 & 0xff000000 (display class), IOProbeScore 60000
personality.finding: the personality matches 8086:4680 as an Intel display-class PCI device, so attachment does not depend on a hard-coded device ID

binary.amfi_relaxed_by_boot_arg: amfi=0x80 is present in both the safe and the test boot configurations
binary.segments: __TEXT 0xac2000 vmsize, __DATA 0x113000, __LINKEDIT 0x187000; LC_SYMTAB, LC_DYSYMTAB and LC_UUID present

preflight_strength.what_it_does: the CI preflight copies the candidate into a temporary repository, runs kmutil create against the runner's real BootKernelExtensions.kc with --allow-missing-kdk, requires the create to succeed, then kmutil inspect verifies com.nullmoth.NMXGPU is in the produced collection
limits: the runner is macOS 15.5 while the target is 15.7.9; KPI 8.0 libraries are stable but this is not the target build
the temporary collection is deliberately never installed, so the real collection for the test boot is built at prepare time on the target

loaded_version_check_as_implemented.method: read run-probe.sh; the check is part of the packaged test path, not something the user must do by hand
kext_identity: before any probe, run-probe.sh requires the staged NMXGPU Mach-O and extracts its x86_64 LC_UUID
it then reads kextstat -l -b com.nullmoth.NMXGPU, requires exactly one table row with a valid UUID, and fails unless that UUID equals the staged binary's UUID
the bundle name and UUID are appended to loaded-UUIDs.txt and the binary sha256 to payload-SHA256SUMS, so the report carries what was actually loaded
userland_identity: the staged runtime directory is walked and every file is hashed into payload-SHA256SUMS

the ICD is rewritten per session with an absolute library_path to the staged libvulkan_intel.dylib, so the loader never searches globally and the relative-path hazard in the shipped intel_icd.json is avoided
the probe is invoked with --device-id 0x4680, so a different device is rejected rather than tested

vulkan_payload_check.icd_shipped: intel_icd.json with library_path ./libvulkan_intel.dylib (relative to its own directory)
vulkan_payload_check.icd_used: rewritten to an absolute path at the staged runtime directory

dylib_install_names.libvulkan_intel.dylib: @loader_path/libvulkan_intel.dylib, loading @loader_path/libdrm.2.dylib plus libSystem, libz and libc++

vulkan_payload_check.finding: no runner path survives in any install name, so the bundle is self-contained; the shader verify.comp.spv (2060 bytes) ships beside the probe
vulkan_payload_check.probe_arguments: --device-id 0x4680 --count 4099 --iterations 3 --deadline 45, with an outer runner deadline of 55 seconds

the probe's first lines, its FAIL and mismatch lines
the port's own NMX DRM discovery lines, which say whether any DRM node could be opened
panic headline, panicked task and the first frames

lines: NMX DRM discovery path=/dev/dri/renderD128 stage=open result=-19 type=0 index=0 bdf=0000:00:00.0 pci=0000:0000
NMX DRM discovery path=/dev/dri/card0 stage=open result=-13 type=0 index=0 bdf=0000:00:00.0 pci=0000:0000
Vulkan Loader ERROR: setup_loader_term_phys_devs: Failed to detect any valid GPUs in the current config

decoded.renderD128 open: -19 is ENODEV: the render node exists but opening it failed inside the driver, not on permissions
decoded.card0 open: -13 is EACCES: the primary node is intentionally root only (nmx_drm_os.c creates primary nodes 0600 and render/accel nodes 0666), and the probe runs as the ordinary user
decoded.bdf/pci 0000:0000: no PCI identity was recovered for either node in that build
decoded.net effect: the Vulkan loader found zero physical devices and returned VK_ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED (-3), so no Vulkan device, submission, fence wait or readback happened at all

discovery_signature_20261021.what_it_reframes: the last target failure was not a compute or completion failure: the MVP is blocked at DRM node discovery/open, upstream of every step T2 to T7 reviewed
discovery_signature_20261021.what_changed_afterwards: the opened-fd identity and cross-node/minor identity work landed after those runs, so r16 may open the node; if the same -19 reappears the next step is the node open path, not compute

discovery_open_path_check.question: is the -19 the last target run hit still reachable in the current tree
where_ENODEV_can_come_from: linux_dev_fdopen returns ENODEV when the cdev's si_drv1 is NULL or the file has no vnode and then nmx_cdev_open prints 'NullMoth devfs: open id=... path=... callback=... error=-19'
drm_open returns ENODEV when the minor it is asked for is not registered
current_tree_state: make_dev_va stores si_drv1 from mda_si_drv1 (override/src/nmx_linux_cdev.c:74) and drm_dev_alias passes the linux_cdev (override/src/nmx_drm_os.c:114), so the guard's first condition is satisfied
nmx_cdev_open installs f_vnode on the file before calling d_fdopen (override/src/nmx_linux_cdev.c:285), so the second condition is satisfied

minor->dev is set when the minor is allocated (drm_drv.c:154) and the device node is only created later, from drm_sysfs_device_add during registration (drm_sysfs.c:380), so an open cannot find an unbound minor through that route
node creation prints on failure and nmx_cdev_open prints on any callback error, so a refusal through this layer leaves a kernel log line
r14_evidence: the captured kernel streams contain 'NullMoth xkpi: 8086:4680: matched by drmn/8086', so the device matched
they contain no 'NullMoth devfs: open' line, so the -19 did not report through the port's own failure path
conclusion: the -19 cannot be attributed to a current-code path from this evidence; either that build lacked the print or the refusal came from the devfs layer before nmx_cdev_open
discovery_open_path_check.discriminator_for_the_next_run: if a device open is refused again, the presence of the port's own 'NullMoth devfs: open ... error=' line says which callback refused it; its absence, in a report that did capture kernel streams, says the refusal happened before the port's open path. The analyzer now separates that from the case where no streams were captured at all, where absence proves nothing.

what_stage_open_proves.reading: the helper starts with stage="open", calls open(O_RDWR|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW), and on failure jumps straight to the summary that prints stage and result; every later step reassigns stage to NODE_INFO, logical-name or PCIINFO before failing
what_stage_open_proves.consequence: the r14 line 'stage=open result=-19' can only have been produced by the open() call itself, so the PCIINFO and NODE_INFO hypotheses are excluded by the code

independent_review.method: a second reviewer, separate context, traced the open path through nmx_devfs.cpp, nmx_linux_cdev.c, nmx_drm_os.c and linux_compat.c and enumerated every ENODEV site
findings: nmx_devfs.cpp contains no ENODEV at all; its failures are ENXIO, EFAULT, EINVAL and ENOMEM, so the XNU glue cannot produce -19
the only open-path ENODEV in the port is linux_dev_fdopen's si_drv1/vnode guard, and it is unreachable for a node that exists because both fields are set before the callback
any error returned through that path is printed twice, by linux_dev_fdopen's caller and by the driver-open wrapper
the remaining reachable source of open(2) == ENODEV is drm_minor_acquire finding no entry for the minor, i.e. the node exists but the render minor was never registered, or was unregistered
independent_review.why_the_missing_log_line_is_not_evidence: the failing boot's captured kernel stream in the r14 report is one of the 293-byte ones that carry only the filter header, so the absence of the port's failure line there says nothing either way
independent_review.discriminator_for_the_next_run: grep the new report's kernel streams for 'NullMoth devfs: open id=': present with error=19 means the driver's open refused and the render minor was not registered; absent, in a report that did capture streams, means open(2) was refused before the port's callback and the XNU devfs layer is the place to look. A root open of /dev/dri/card0 separates 'no minor registered at all' from 'render minor missing'.

strongest_current_hypothesis.evidence: across the whole r14 report - 33 kernel-stream captures and 268 dmesg snapshots - there is not one 'NullMoth devfs: open' line, and the dmesg snapshots demonstrably do carry the port's printf output
strongest_current_hypothesis.inference: the ENODEV therefore did not travel through the port's device-open path, which prints twice on every error; the refusal came from below it, in the XNU devfs layer, or the path being opened was not the node the port created
what_it_rules_out: drm_minor_acquire finding no registered render minor, which would have printed
the linux_dev_fdopen guard, which would also have printed
caveats: dmesg is a ring buffer, so a very early line could have rolled off before the first snapshot
the probe's own discovery line proves open(2) failed with errno 19, not that the port was bypassed; both facts together are what narrow it
strongest_current_hypothesis.next_step_if_reproduced: one print at the top of nmx_open recording the minor would settle whether XNU reaches the port's callback at all. That needs a kext rebuild and a new package, so it is held until the next run shows the same signature

stale_node_after_reload.idea: a /dev/dri node left over from an earlier kext load would point at a major whose cdevsw is gone, so open would fail with ENODEV and nothing in the port would print
checked: destroy_dev clears c->nmx_node, sets nmx_gone, and calls nmx_xnu_devfs_remove
nmx_xnu_devfs_remove calls devfs_remove(handle) and clears both the handle and the cookie slot
nmx_xnu_devfs_fini only removes the cdevsw, so it relies on every cdev having been destroyed first, which is the normal teardown order
stale_node_after_reload.verdict: unlikely on the documented flow: the test boot loads the kext once and the nodes are created and removed through these paths

clone_minor_leak.idea: clone_minor returns 0 for DEVFS_CLONE_FREE without clearing its table, so each open could permanently consume a minor until allocation fails
checked: nmx_open clears g_open_node[m] on any error
nmx_close clears g_open_node[m] for every clone minor on close

gone_device.idea: opening a node whose cdev was destroyed returns the port's 'gone' error
checked: nmx_cdev_open returns an error for a gone cdev, and that error is printed by the same two call sites

discovery_open_path_check.current_state: with the port's own paths ruled out both by source (they print or are unreachable) and by the captured logs (no such line in 33 streams or 268 dmesg snapshots), two explanations remain: XNU devfs refuses the open before d_open, or the path being opened is not the node this kext instance created. Both need a target observation, and the next run's report discriminates them by whether any port-side line appears at all.

Bringing only the report folder would show that the run stopped without saying where

analyzer_tested_on_both_outcomes.failure_report: r14 with its panic file: reproduces the panic verdict, lists the sessions and the discovery lines, and reports that no port-side open failure line exists across 33 captured streams
analyzer_tested_on_both_outcomes.success_report: a synthetic report with a COMPUTE_READBACK_VERIFIED probe log and coordinator_exit=0: verdict reports the marker instead of a failure

dmesg_is_a_second_record_of_the_kernel_l.finding: the collector writes two independent records of the kernel log: the log-stream captures and periodic dmesg snapshots that are 128 KB each. The r14 report holds 33 stream files and 268 dmesg snapshots, and the dmesg ones are full of the port's own NullMoth trace and dbg lines, so kernel printf is captured there even when a stream file is only its header
dmesg_is_a_second_record_of_the_kernel_l.tool_change: the analyzer now scans both, and reports how many of each it read
dmesg_is_a_second_record_of_the_kernel_l.why_it_mattered: before this, the analyzer only read kernel-stream.txt. In r14 that file was empty for the failing boot, which is why the absence of the port's open-failure line looked like no evidence at all

boot_flag_delivery_check.question: does the test boot actually receive nmxintel=1, or can NVRAM keep an older -nvoff
boot_flag_delivery_check.how_boot_args_reach_the_kernel: OpenCore writes NVRAM under 7C436110-AB2A-4BBB-A880-FE41995C9F82. Its own log shows it comparing the existing value with the config value ('Not deleting NVRAM ... matches add', then 'ignored, exists'), which only happens because the config carries a Delete entry for boot-args

verified_in_both_configs.test_add: -v debug=0x100 keepsyms=1 -igfxvesa alcid=11 amfi=0x80 ipc_control_port_options=0 nmxintel=1 nmxdiagdelay=180

boot_flag_delivery_check.conclusion: because boot-args is deleted and re-added with WriteFlash, switching the USB to the test config replaces the NVRAM value rather than being ignored, so the test boot should see nmxintel=1 and no -nvoff
boot_flag_delivery_check.why_it_mattered: had the Delete entry been missing, OpenCore would have kept the existing -nvoff and session-user.sh would have refused with 'This is not the prepared Intel test boot', wasting the hardware round
boot_flag_delivery_check.limit: this is the configuration's intent; the boot that runs is the only proof, and the session refuses rather than proceeding wrong if it is missing
